about: Starting knowledge per market and position, before any CV archive has been analysed. Every note is a [PRIOR]: recruiter knowledge to be confirmed or overturned by measure_markets.py once real CVs are in. Patterns match accent-free, lowercase text.

playbooks.label: Belgium · Accounting

conventions.label: ITAA status
conventions.why: The Belgian professional body for accountants and tax advisers (IEC and IPCF merged into ITAA in 2019). Clients read it as a level: trainee, certified accountant, tax adviser.

conventions.label: Full-cycle bookkeeping ("comptabilité de A à Z")
conventions.pattern: de a a z|van a tot z|a to z|full[- ]cycle
conventions.why: The phrase Belgian clients look for: the person can run the books alone, from entry to annual accounts.

conventions.label: Accounting-firm experience (fiduciaire / boekhoudkantoor)
conventions.why: Firm experience means many clients, many sectors and deadline discipline. SMEs value it; it is a different profile from in-house.

conventions.label: VAT returns (TVA / btw), client listing
conventions.why: Monthly or quarterly VAT is core Belgian work; Intervat is the filing platform.

conventions.label: Tax returns (ISOC / IPP, vennootschapsbelasting)
conventions.why: Separates bookkeepers from people who can close and file.

conventions.label: Annual accounts filed with the National Bank (BNB / NBB)
conventions.why: Filing the annual accounts is the end of the cycle; mentioning it proves the full cycle.

conventions.label: Belgian chart of accounts (PCMN / MAR)
conventions.why: Signals Belgian GAAP rather than IFRS or French PCG.

conventions.label: Payroll via a social secretariat
conventions.why: In Belgium payroll runs through a social secretariat; accountants check it rather than compute it.

conventions.label: Belgian accounting software
conventions.why: Clients filter on the package they run. Winbooks, BOB and Exact are the common ones.

notes.text: Say whether the experience is in a fiduciaire or in-house: clients hire for one or the other.
State the ITAA stage precisely (trainee, certified, tax adviser). Never translate the acronym.
If the candidate did the books alone, use the local phrase: comptabilité de A à Z / boekhouding van A tot Z.
Name the software. It is often the first filter.
Brussels and Wallonia clients read French; Flanders reads Dutch. Bilingual candidates are worth flagging up front.

avoid: Calling a Belgian fiduciaire a 'cabinet': that is French usage.
French titles such as expert-comptable diplômé or DCG/DSCG unless the candidate really holds them.
IFRS as a headline unless the role is group or subsidiary reporting.

playbooks.label: Luxembourg · Accounting

conventions.label: Fund accounting (UCITS, AIF, NAV)
conventions.why: The fund industry is a large share of accounting jobs in Luxembourg.

conventions.label: CSSF regulatory reporting
conventions.why: The Luxembourg financial regulator; reporting experience is a strong signal.

conventions.label: Lux GAAP / IFRS
conventions.why: Clients want to know which standard the candidate has closed under.

conventions.label: RCS / eCDF filing
conventions.why: Local filing platforms; proves hands-on Luxembourg closing.

notes.text: English is the default working language in fund services; state French and German levels separately.
Say whether the experience is fund, corporate (Soparfi) or SME: they are different markets.

avoid: Belgian-specific terms (ITAA, Winbooks, BNB) as selling points in Luxembourg.

playbooks.label: France · Accounting

conventions.label: DCG / DSCG / DEC
conventions.why: The French qualification ladder; clients read the level from it.

notes.text: French CVs often run to two pages with a longer education section; keep the Zig page to one.

avoid: Belgian terms (fiduciaire, ITAA, TVA listing) for French clients.

conventions.label: Freelance status (indépendant / zelfstandige, own company)
conventions.why: Belgian IT contracting often runs through the consultant's own company; clients want to know how to contract.

conventions.label: Named end clients
conventions.why: Belgian consultants list missions per end client; clients read the sector from them.

conventions.label: Language levels (CEFR)
conventions.why: Belgian clients expect FR/NL/EN levels, ideally A1-C2.

notes.text: Give the daily rate and whether the candidate invoices through a company.
English CVs are normal in IT; the Zig page can still follow the contact's language.
